Microsoft's [Zero Trust Assessment](https://github.com/microsoft/zerotrustassessment)
runs hundreds of read-only checks against your Entra / Intune / Azure / Purview
tenant and writes a `ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html`. That report is excellent
for browsing but hard to *act on* as a team. This guide walks you — entirely
from PowerShell — through turning it into:

- an **Excel dashboard** (charts + pillar × risk heatmap, findings grouped by
  pillar, **severity scored 0–100**, and a **remediation priority** P1–P4 with
  quick-wins called out), and
- a **Power BI-ready CSV** (one tidy row per check, every derived column).

::: {.callout-important}
## Handle the output as Controlled data
The assessment report and everything derived from it contain sensitive tenant
configuration — effectively a map of where you are weak. Keep all input and
output **inside your authorization boundary**, share only with authorized
personnel, and **do not publish raw findings**. Remediation guidance is
**advisory**: apply changes only through your normal change-control process.
:::

## What you get

| Output | Description |
|---|---|
| `…-dashboard.xlsx` | **Dashboard** sheet with four embedded charts; **Findings** (ranked, severity color-scale, P1–P4 fills); **By Pillar**; **All Tests**; **Methodology** (the exact scoring, documented). |
| `charts\*.png` | The individual charts (status, findings-by-pillar, pillar × risk heatmap, severity × effort remediation quadrant). |
| `…-powerbi.csv` | One row per check with severity, priority, applicability, and SKU columns — import directly into Power BI. |

## Prerequisites

- **PowerShell 7+** — [install guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/scripting/install/installing-powershell).
- **Python 3.11+** on `PATH`.
- **The UIAO toolkit** (provides the `uiao` command): `pip install uiao` from the
  repository, which brings in the `openpyxl` and `matplotlib` dependencies the
  dashboard needs.
- A **`ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html`** (or `.json`) from a completed assessment
  run — produced in Step 1 below.

```powershell
# one-time: confirm the toolkit is available
uiao --version
uiao zta --help
```

## Step 1 — Run the Zero Trust Assessment

If you have not already produced a report, run the assessment (read-only). The
first run needs a Global Administrator to consent; later runs can use Global
Reader. See Microsoft's [get-started guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/security/zero-trust/assessment/get-started).

```powershell
Install-Module ZeroTrustAssessment -Scope CurrentUser
Connect-ZtAssessment
Invoke-ZtAssessment            # writes .\ZeroTrustReport\ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html
```

::: {.callout-note}
The assessment can take a while on large tenants. The HTML it opens by default
already embeds the full dataset — the dashboard reads it directly, so you do
**not** need a separate JSON export.
:::

## Step 2 — Generate the dashboard

Download **`Invoke-ZtDashboard.ps1`** (see [Downloads](#downloads)) and run it
against the report:

```powershell
.\Invoke-ZtDashboard.ps1 -ReportPath .\ZeroTrustReport\ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html -OutputDirectory .\zt-dashboard
```

That is a thin wrapper over the toolkit; the equivalent direct call is:

```powershell
uiao zta dashboard --input .\ZeroTrustReport\ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html --out-dir .\zt-dashboard
```

You can also produce the lighter text/CSV digests (executive summary, Markdown,
worklist) with:

```powershell
uiao zta digest --input .\ZeroTrustReport\ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html --out-dir .\zt-digest
```

## Reading the dashboard

- **Outcomes are recomputed from the per-test results.** The report's own
  summary block is intentionally ignored because it does not reconcile.
- **Only `Failed` and `Investigate` are findings.** `Skipped` (not applicable /
  unlicensed) and `Planned` (a check Microsoft has not implemented yet) are shown
  but are **not** gaps — don't chase them.
- **Severity (0–100)** = risk × status weighting. **Priority** = severity ÷
  effort, so a high-severity, low-effort check (a *quick win*) outranks a
  high-severity, high-effort one. Buckets: **P1 ≥ 50, P2 ≥ 30, P3 ≥ 15, P4 > 0**.
- The **Findings** sheet is your worklist — sorted P1 first, severity color-scaled.
- The **remediation quadrant** chart splits findings into quick-wins (top-left)
  vs major projects (top-right).

::: {.callout-warning}
## Verify boundary scope before acting
Many checks require premium / P2-class SKUs (flagged in the **ApplicabilityNote**
column). In a GCC / FedRAMP Moderate tenant some of those capabilities may not be
available or authorized — so a "skipped" or "failed" premium check may not be a
real gap. Confirm the SKU applies in your boundary before scoring it as one.
:::

## Power BI quickstart

1. Power BI Desktop → **Get Data → Text/CSV** → select `…-powerbi.csv`.
2. It's already tidy (one row per check). Build visuals directly — e.g. a matrix
   of `Pillar` × `Status`, a bar of `PriorityBucket`, or a card for count of
   `IsFinding = yes`.
3. Useful measures: count of findings (`IsFinding = "yes"`), average
   `SeverityScore` by `Pillar`, P1 count by `Pillar`.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `uiao: command not found` | The toolkit isn't installed/active. `pip install uiao`, or the wrapper will fall back to `python -m uiao.cli.app` if Python is on `PATH`. |
| Unicode / `cp1252` errors in the console | Run `"$env:PYTHONUTF8 = 1"` before invoking, or use PowerShell 7. |
| `could not locate an embedded reportData object` | The input isn't a Zero Trust Assessment report — point `-ReportPath` at the real `…Report.html` or a `.json` export. |
